class_name: 起点-極端例-ヲハジメトシテ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Names the leading or most representative member of a set and implies that the rest follow (校長をはじめとして先生方が並ぶ, 京都をはじめとする古都), so the noun it marks should genuinely rank first. The sibling など only offers a sample and can sound offhand, while をはじめとして ranks explicitly. Register is written and ceremonial, and the clipped をはじめ is by far the most common shape.

examples.ruby: 校長[こうちょう]をはじめとして、先生[せんせい]方[がた]が壇上[だんじょう]に並[なら]んだ。
examples.english: Led by the principal, the teachers lined up on the stage.

examples.ruby: 京都[きょうと]をはじめとする古都[こと]には、外国[がいこく]からの客[きゃく]が多[おお]い。
examples.english: The ancient capitals, Kyoto foremost among them, draw many visitors from abroad.

examples.ruby: 小麦[こむぎ]をはじめ、輸入[ゆにゅう]品[ひん]の値段[ねだん]が上[あ]がり続[つづ]けている。
examples.english: Starting with wheat, the prices of imported goods just keep climbing.

patterns.usage_note: Offers a non-exhaustive sample: the item named is representative, and comparable things are meant to be inferred (パンやジャムなどを買う, 頭痛やめまいなどの症状). The sibling をはじめとして instead ranks its noun first in the set. It attaches to nouns, to dictionary-form verbs and i-adjectives, and to だ/た, and it also softens what it names (お茶などいかがですか); with a negative predicate it turns dismissive (謝る気などない).

examples.ruby: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]はパンやジャムなどを買[か]いに行[い]く。
examples.english: On my days off I go out for bread, jam, that sort of thing.

examples.ruby: 週末[しゅうまつ]は本[ほん]を読[よ]むなどして静[しず]かに過[す]ごした。
examples.english: I spent a quiet weekend reading and the like.

examples.ruby: 頭痛[ずつう]やめまいなどの症状[しょうじょう]が続[つづ]いている。
examples.english: Symptoms such as headaches and dizziness have been persisting.
